drills.label: Cold open
drills.question_line: SAM: A media company's procurement team shows you a slide prepared this week.
drills.answer_line: SAM: So A collapses: in January there is no list-price gap.
drills.stem: A slide prepared this week compares Gemini 4 Carbon at $2/$10 per M tokens with Claude Opus 5.5 at $4/$20 and recommends a three-year Carbon commitment from January, on price. What is the best advice?

options.A: Agree: Carbon is half the price
options.B: Redo the comparison at January's prices, then on cost per task from an eval on their own work
options.C: Set price aside and pick Claude Fable 5.2, because it leads the independent index
options.D: Sign before the introductory price ends, to lock it in

drills.why: Carbon's $2/$10 is introductory and ends 30 Nov 2026; from 1 Dec it is $4/$20, the same as Opus 5.5. Then compare cost per task: on Artificial Analysis (14 Nov 2026) Carbon scored 60 vs Opus 59 at about half the cost per task, so the eval may pick Carbon. C ignores the price question; D bets three years on a promotion.

drills.label: Drill
drills.question_line: SAM: Pause here and answer before we go on. Choose two. An insurer choosing a coding agent
drills.answer_line: SAM: Both. B is independent, dated and priced
drills.stem: Choose two. An insurer choosing a coding agent has five pieces of evidence. Which two should carry the most weight?

options.A: A vendor-reported Terminal-Bench score comparing the vendor's new model with a rival's previous one
options.B: The Artificial Analysis index read this week, with cost per task beside each score
options.D: A two-week pilot on the insurer's own repositories and tickets
options.E: First place on Arena's text board

drills.why: B is independent, dated and priced; D measures the customer's own work. A is vendor-reported against an older rival, C is a retired benchmark with flawed tests, E measures chat preference.

drills.label: Drill
drills.question_line: SAM: Pause here and answer before we go on. A retailer classifies millions of product listings a month.
drills.answer_line: SAM: That is the take-the-biggest-model reflex.
drills.stem: Mid-tier quality is enough, cost per task is the constraint, and spend must draw down the AWS commitment. What do you recommend?

options.A: Test GPT-6.1 Sol against Claude Sonnet 5.5, both on Amazon Bedrock, on their own listings; choose on cost per correct result
options.B: Claude Fable 5.2, because it leads the independent index
options.C: Gemini 3.8 Flash at its promotional price, for two years
options.D: Opus 5.5, because Menlo shows most enterprise spend goes to Anthropic

drills.why: Both are on Bedrock, so both draw down the AWS commit. On Artificial Analysis (14 Nov 2026) Sol matched Sonnet's score of 55 at about one-eighth the cost per task. B has the highest cost per task of the index leaders; C is off their cloud and its promo ends 31 Dec 2026; D picks from a survey, not the workload.

drills.label: Drill
drills.question_line: SAM: Pause here and answer before we go on. For each statement, say true or false, as of November fourteenth.
drills.answer_line: SAM: All five. Astra is ten and fifty to Fable's eight and forty.
drills.prompt: True or false, as of 14 Nov 2026? 1) GPT-6 Astra's list price is below Claude Fable 5.2's. 2) Google's 9% in the Menlo report includes Workspace bundles. 3) A team can still build a new agent in OpenAI's Agent Builder canvas in December. 4) Gemini 4 Carbon is first on Arena's text board, on a preliminary score. 5) Claude Code was the most-used coding agent in Stack Overflow's 2026 survey.
drills.answer: 1) False: $10/$50 vs $8/$40. 2) False: API spend only. 3) False: Agent Builder goes 30 Nov 2026. 4) True (11 Nov 2026). 5) True: 66% vs Copilot 59%.

drills.question_line: SAM: Recall first. Pause and name the four segments
drills.prompt: Name the four segments, and one number from each you would recheck before quoting.
drills.answer: Line-ups and prices: Carbon's introductory rate. Benchmarks: the Artificial Analysis index. Market share: Menlo's 55%. Shutdowns: Agent Builder, 30 November.
